With `return_logprob` and no top-k or token-id logprob requests, the standard sampling path built `torch.log(probs)` over `[bs, vocab]` and clamped the whole tensor in place, only to gather one value per row. title: [Perf] Broadcast single-image DP vision embedding instead of pad-to-max all-gather
body:
For a single-image request exactly one rank holds the embedding, so the symmetric all-gather moves `tp_size x max_len` rows of which `(tp_size-1)/tp_size` is padding, and every rank allocates a `tp_size`-times-larger buffer. Broadcast from the owner rank instead — bit-identical, one copy instead of `tp_size`.

Verified on 8x B300, 3 runs: all ranks bitwise-equal to both the all-gather result and ground truth; all-gather 0.69ms -> broadcast 0.09ms (7.6x) at `[5476, 4096]` bf16 (~45MB). Reproducer: `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 test/manual/vlm/verify_single_image_gather.py`.

Multi-image and `tp_size == 1` paths are untouched.

title: feat: [2/2][DeepEP] Add waterfill load balancing for shared expert dispatch
body:
## Motivation

In DeepSeek V3/R1 with expert parallelism (EP), each rank processes a subset of routed experts plus the **full** shared expert. Since every token must visit the shared expert, it creates a fixed compute load on all ranks regardless of routed expert distribution. When routed expert load is imbalanced across ranks (common with skewed token distributions), the shared expert amplifies the bottleneck on already-overloaded ranks.
**Waterfill** addresses this by treating the shared expert as an additional routed expert (the "9th expert" per rank) and dispatching it to the **least-loaded** rank via DeepEP, effectively filling the load gap like water filling a container. This converts the shared expert from a fixed per-rank cost into a dynamic load-balancing lever.

body:
Fixes #47282

**Root cause:** After #46278 fixed the store-side compute-vs-store race, a second independent race remained on the **load** path. When a GPU block is freed and immediately reallocated as a load destination, the load DMA (on the dedicated low-priority `load_stream`) can begin overwriting that block while a **previous** request attention computation is still reading it on the compute stream. title: [ROCm][PERF] Enable MiniMax-M3 Indexer CP
body:
## Purpose

Adds **indexer-only context parallelism** for the MiniMax-M3 lightning indexer on ROCm (gfx950), opt-in behind `--attention-config '{"indexer_cp": true}'`. Under tensor parallelism each rank owns one index head and scores *every*
128-token block, so at long context every rank re-reads the whole index cache on every decode step and that cost grows linearly with the context. This PR inverts the split: every rank projects **all** index heads and scores **1/P of the
blocks**, then one small exchange gives each rank every shard's candidates for the heads it owns. That turns the index-cache reads into `1/P`, which is the only term here that scales with context.
